```{python}
import sys

from shared.components import chart_card, method_and_sources, prev_next, stat_tile, stat_tiles
from shared.context import load_context
from shared.outputs import read_output
from shared.paths import CASE_STUDIES, REPO_URL, ROOT

STUDY = CASE_STUDIES / "05_agrifood_processing"
sys.path.insert(0, str(STUDY / "analysis"))
import figures as F  # noqa: E402

series, prov_series, notes_series = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "agrifood_series.csv")
trend, prov_trend, notes_trend = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "agrifood_categories_2010_2013.csv")
cats, prov_cats, notes_cats = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "agrifood_categories_2013.csv")
dist, prov_dist, notes_dist = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "agrifood_districts_2013.csv")
ctx = load_context(STUDY / "context.yml")  # institutional reports, background only (policy §7)

FIRST, LAST = int(series.year.min()), int(series.year.max())
PREV = LAST - 1
s = series.set_index("year")
m = F.millions
growth = s.loc[PREV, "comparable_bnd"] / s.loc[FIRST, "comparable_bnd"]
# The text says value rose every year to PREV; stop the build rather than publish it if not.
assert s.loc[:PREV, "comparable_bnd"].is_monotonic_increasing, "Rewrite 'rose every year'."
fall = (s.loc[LAST, "comparable_bnd"] / s.loc[PREV, "comparable_bnd"] - 1) * 100
new_share = s.loc[LAST, "new_category_bnd"] / s.loc[LAST, "total_bnd"] * 100
crop_06, crop_08 = s.loc[2006, "crop_bnd"], s.loc[2008, "crop_bnd"]
t = trend.pivot(index="category", columns="year", values="value_bnd")
BAKERY, MEAT, DRINKS, TRAD = "Biscuits & bakery", "Meat products", "Mineral water & soft drinks", "Traditional foods"
c = cats.set_index("category")
biz_share = c.businesses / c.businesses.sum() * 100
d = dist.set_index("district")
bm = d.loc["Brunei-Muara"]


def pct(v, digits=0):
    return f"{v:.{digits}f}%"


def size(v, digits=0):
    """Size of a rise or fall for prose ("fell 18%"), where the verb carries the sign."""
    return f"{abs(v):.{digits}f}%"
```

::: {.study-intro}
This case study looks at Brunei's **agrifood processing industry**, the businesses that turn
farm and fishery produce into food products such as bread, biscuits, drinks and meat products.
It uses the Ministry of Industry and Primary Resources' *agrimakanan* (agrifood) tables, which
cover **2004 to 2013**. Although published in 2025, the data ends in 2013. It shows **what
changed, not why**.

It asks two questions, answered in the conclusion:

1. **How did the industry's market value change from 2004 to 2013?**
2. **What did it make in 2013, and where was it based?**
:::

```{python}
stat_tiles(
    stat_tile(f"Market value, {FIRST} → {PREV}", f"{growth:.1f}×", "", f"{m(s.loc[FIRST, 'comparable_bnd'])} → {m(s.loc[PREV, 'comparable_bnd'])}"),
    stat_tile(f"Market value, {LAST}", m(s.loc[LAST, "total_bnd"]), "", f"incl. {m(s.loc[LAST, 'new_category_bnd'])} from a category first counted in {LAST}"),
    stat_tile(f"Without that category, {PREV} → {LAST}", f"−{size(fall)}", "", f"{m(s.loc[PREV, 'comparable_bnd'])} → {m(s.loc[LAST, 'comparable_bnd'])}"),
)
```

```{python}
fig, table = F.series_chart(series)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Market value rose every year to {PREV}; in {LAST}, a newly counted category hid a fall",
    subtitle=f"Market value of processed agrifood products, B$ million, current prices · {FIRST}–{LAST} · grey: fast or instant food, first counted in {LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Stacked bar chart. Market value rises from {m(s.loc[FIRST, 'comparable_bnd'])} in "
        f"{FIRST} to {m(s.loc[PREV, 'comparable_bnd'])} in {PREV}. In {LAST}, the categories "
        f"counted every year fall to {m(s.loc[LAST, 'comparable_bnd'])}, and a new grey segment "
        f"of {m(s.loc[LAST, 'new_category_bnd'])} brings the total to {m(s.loc[LAST, 'total_bnd'])}."
    ),
    provenance=prov_series,
    table=table,
)
```

## Market value, 2004–2013

The industry's market value rose every year from `{python} FIRST` to `{python} PREV`, from
`{python} m(s.loc[FIRST, "comparable_bnd"])` to `{python} m(s.loc[PREV, "comparable_bnd"])`,
`{python} f"{growth:.1f}×"` as much. The biggest rise came in 2007–2008, when crop-based
products went from `{python} m(crop_06)` (2006) to `{python} m(crop_08)` (2008).

**In `{python} LAST`, the total jumped to `{python} m(s.loc[LAST, "total_bnd"])`, but
`{python} pct(new_share)` of that came from "Makanan Segera" (fast or instant food), a category
that appears for the first time that year.** Without it, the categories counted every year
fell `{python} size(fall)`, to `{python} m(s.loc[LAST, "comparable_bnd"])`.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Livestock-based and crop-based"}
The Ministry splits the industry into **livestock-based** products (meat products, and from
2013 fast or instant food) and **crop-based** products (everything else, including fish
products). Values are in current Brunei dollars, not adjusted for inflation.
:::

## What was made, 2012–2013

```{python}
fig, table = F.categories_chart(trend, PREV, LAST)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Biscuits & bakery fell from {m(t.loc[BAKERY, PREV])} to {m(t.loc[BAKERY, LAST])} in {LAST}",
    subtitle=f"Market value by product category, B$ million · {PREV} and {LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Bar chart of market value by category for {PREV} and {LAST}. Biscuits and bakery fall "
        f"from {m(t.loc[BAKERY, PREV])} to {m(t.loc[BAKERY, LAST])}; meat products from "
        f"{m(t.loc[MEAT, PREV])} to {m(t.loc[MEAT, LAST])}; fast or instant food appears at "
        f"{m(t.loc[F.NEW, LAST])}. Most other categories are under B$3 million."
    ),
    provenance=prov_trend,
    table=table,
    height=520,
)
```

Biscuits & bakery was the largest category counted every year, but fell from
`{python} m(t.loc[BAKERY, PREV])` to `{python} m(t.loc[BAKERY, LAST])`. Meat products also fell,
from `{python} m(t.loc[MEAT, PREV])` to `{python} m(t.loc[MEAT, LAST])`. Mineral water & soft
drinks held at about `{python} m(t.loc[DRINKS, LAST], 0)`.

## Many small producers, 2013

```{python}
fig, table = F.producers_chart(cats)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Traditional foods had the most businesses but {pct(c.loc[TRAD, 'share_pct'], 1)} of the market value",
    subtitle=f"Each product category's share of businesses* and of market value (%) · {LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Two bar charts by category. Traditional foods have {pct(biz_share[TRAD])} of businesses "
        f"but {pct(c.loc[TRAD, 'share_pct'], 1)} of market value. Fast or instant food has "
        f"{pct(biz_share[F.NEW])} of businesses and {pct(c.loc[F.NEW, 'share_pct'])} of value."
    ),
    provenance=prov_cats,
    table=table,
    height=520,
    mobile_fig=F.producers_chart(cats, cols=1)[0],
    mobile_height=900,
)
```

Market value was concentrated in a few categories. In `{python} LAST`,
`{python} int(c.loc[TRAD, "businesses"])` businesses made traditional foods, the most of any
category, but they produced `{python} pct(c.loc[TRAD, "share_pct"], 1)` of the market value.
`{python} int(c.loc[F.NEW, "businesses"])` businesses made fast or instant food, which was
`{python} pct(c.loc[F.NEW, "share_pct"])` of the value.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="*How businesses are counted"}
**A business that makes several kinds of product is counted once in each category**, so the
category counts add up to more than the number of businesses (the district table gives
`{python} int(d.businesses.sum())` in total). Values for a single district and category aren't
shown, because many rest on fewer than 5 businesses and could reveal one firm's sales.
:::

## Where the industry was, 2013

```{python}
fig, table = F.districts_chart(dist)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Brunei-Muara had {pct(bm.businesses_share_pct)} of businesses but {pct(bm.value_bnd_share_pct)} of the market value",
    subtitle=f"Each district's share of agrifood businesses, employees and market value (%) · {LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Three bar charts by district. Brunei-Muara: {pct(bm.businesses_share_pct)} of businesses, "
        f"{pct(bm.employees_share_pct)} of employees, {pct(bm.value_bnd_share_pct)} of market value. "
        f"Temburong: {pct(d.loc['Temburong', 'businesses_share_pct'])} of businesses but "
        f"{pct(d.loc['Temburong', 'value_bnd_share_pct'], 1)} of value."
    ),
    provenance=prov_dist,
    table=table,
    height=260,
    mobile_fig=F.districts_chart(dist, cols=1)[0],
    mobile_height=620,
)
```

**Brunei-Muara accounted for `{python} pct(bm.value_bnd_share_pct)` of the industry's market
value in `{python} LAST`**, with `{python} pct(bm.businesses_share_pct)` of its businesses and
`{python} pct(bm.employees_share_pct)` of its employees. Temburong had
`{python} int(d.loc["Temburong", "businesses"])` businesses, more than Tutong or Belait, but the
smallest share of the value.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="What was reported at the time, and since"}
These come from institutional reports, not from the data above. No peer-reviewed study of the
industry in these years was found.

- **Policy at the time.** Officials of the Department of Agriculture and Agrifood described the
  agrifood industry as developing with small and medium enterprises during the department's
  2008–2013 Medium-Term Strategic Plan. A Small Entrepreneurs Food Incubator Centre supported
  processing, food safety and quality, and the Brunei Halal Brand was set up to reach local and
  overseas markets (`{python} ctx["searca2016"].cite()`).
- **Since 2013.** A 2026 regional report put agri-food processing output at B$110.5 million in
  2015 and about B$172.5 million in 2024. It also found that imported food met over 70% of
  Brunei's food needs in 2024, and that the sector had limited links to the rest of the economy
  (`{python} ctx["khut2026"].cite()`).

**The 2026 report may measure output differently from the Ministry tables used here, so its
figures can't be joined to the chart above.**
:::

## Conclusion

- **How did the industry's market value change from 2004 to 2013?** It rose every year to
  `{python} PREV`, from `{python} m(s.loc[FIRST, "comparable_bnd"])` to
  `{python} m(s.loc[PREV, "comparable_bnd"])` (`{python} f"{growth:.1f}×"`). In
  `{python} LAST`, the published total rose to `{python} m(s.loc[LAST, "total_bnd"])`, but only
  because a new category was counted; the categories counted every year fell
  `{python} size(fall)`, led by biscuits & bakery.
- **What did it make in 2013, and where was it based?** Mostly fast or instant food, biscuits &
  bakery, drinks and meat products, which together made up
  `{python} pct(c.loc[[F.NEW, BAKERY, DRINKS, MEAT], "share_pct"].sum())` of the value. Many
  businesses made traditional foods (`{python} int(c.loc[TRAD, "businesses"])`) and snacks
  (`{python} int(c.loc["Snacks", "businesses"])`), but on a small scale. Almost all of the
  value (`{python} pct(bm.value_bnd_share_pct)`) came from Brunei-Muara.

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" title="What this doesn't tell us"}
<!-- Side note: required on every case study (DESIGN.md §4.1). -->
- **Why.** The data doesn't explain the 2007–2008 rise or the `{python} LAST` fall.
- **Whether `{python} LAST` was real growth.** Fast or instant food may have been made before
  `{python} LAST` without being counted; the source doesn't say.
- **Prices.** Values are in current Brunei dollars, not adjusted for inflation.
- **After `{python} LAST`.** The Ministry tables end in `{python} LAST`. Later figures from
  other reports may use different definitions.
- **Head-counts.** Two published tables give different numbers of businesses and employees
  for `{python} LAST`. The district table is used for totals.
- **Farming.** This is about processed food, not about crops, livestock or fish produced on
  farms.
:::
